label: cache-hit
definition: Share of input tokens served from the prompt cache rather than billed at the full fresh-input rate.
so_what: Below 25 % means sessions run cold — every un-cached token costs 5–10× more than a warm hit. The single biggest lever on total API spend.

insight.warn_msg: Sessions running cold — warm them to cut input cost.

label: burn $/hr
definition: Total API cost divided by observed session span in hours — the fleet's live run rate.
so_what: Tracks runway against usage limits. Spikes signal a runaway agent or an unexpectedly large cold-cache context.

insight.warn_msg: Burn rate elevated — check for runaway runs or cold-cache sessions.

label: idle-run %
definition: Percentage of runs that produced no file edit — context re-reads with no committed output.
so_what: High idle-run % means agents burn tokens without advancing work. Prime target for better event-driven wake scheduling (NORMS §2).

insight.warn_msg: Too many idle runs — agents may be polling or waking on noise.

label: Haiku cost %
definition: Percentage of total token spend going to the Haiku tier (cheapest model).
so_what: Low Haiku % means lightweight tasks are escalating to expensive tiers unnecessarily. Routine tasks should run on Haiku; heavy reasoning on Opus.

insight.warn_msg: Low Haiku usage — lightweight tasks may be over-tiered.

label: verbosity
definition: Output tokens generated per input token consumed. Measures how much agents write relative to what they read.
so_what: Very high verbosity bloats the context window and drives up cost on the next turn. Low verbosity usually means terse, efficient agents.

insight.warn_msg: Agents generating excessive output — future context and cost will balloon.

label: coordination %
definition: Percentage of bus messages that are pure coordination overhead (ACK, STATUS, NUDGE, PING, NOTE, FreeText) rather than substantive typed artifacts.
so_what: High coordination % means the bus is congested with meta-chatter. Every coordination message is cost and latency with no product shipped.

insight.warn_msg: Over half of bus traffic is coordination overhead — look for ACK storms or polling loops.

label: hub Gini
definition: Gini coefficient of outbound message volume across roles. 0 = all roles equally active; 1 = one role sends everything.
so_what: High Gini flags a hub bottleneck — one role acting as traffic concentrator slows the whole fleet whenever it is busy or blocked.

insight.warn_msg: Bus traffic highly concentrated — one role is a bottleneck.

label: handoff p90
definition: 90th-percentile delay between a message being sent and first read — the tail queue latency on the bus.
so_what: Long p90 handoff means messages pile up unread. This is the coordination tax agents pay while waiting for a reply to unblock their next action.

insight.warn_msg: Tail handoff latency high — agents waiting too long for replies.

label: avg cycle
definition: Average time from first to last message on a ticket thread (correlation_id group) in milliseconds.
so_what: Long average cycle time means tickets take many turns to resolve — caused by rework, handoff delays, or stuck challenges.

insight.warn_msg: Tickets averaging over 30 min — check for rework or stuck handoffs.

label: queue depth
definition: Depth of the deepest unread inbox — the number of messages waiting in the busiest blocked role's queue.
so_what: Rising queue depth on a single role is the first signal that an agent is stuck, slow, or ignoring its inbox.

insight.warn_msg: A role has a deep unread queue — agent may be stuck or idle.

label: rework events
definition: Total REVISED + CHALLENGE + REJECT + ESCALATE events on the bus — the aggregate rework signal.
so_what: Each rework event is a failed first-pass. High rework drives up cycle time, API cost, and coordination overhead.

insight.warn_msg: High rework — check AC clarity, TDD discipline, and first-pass quality.

label: zero-bloat score
definition: 0–100 composite of code permanence, low file thrash, healthy test ratio, zero dep growth, and compact diff size. 100 = leanest.
so_what: Below 60 means the codebase is accumulating dead rewrites, bloated diffs, or dependency sprawl — direct NORMS §1 violations.

insight.warn_msg: Zero-bloat score low — check for thrash, dep growth, or thin test ratio.

label: dep lines added
definition: Lines added to dependency manifests (requirements.txt, package.json, pyproject.toml, etc.) in recent commits.
so_what: Every dep line is a new external surface and a future upgrade burden. NORMS §1 mandates justifying each new dependency.

insight.warn_msg: New dependency added — confirm it's justified and no stdlib alternative exists.

label: test:code ratio
definition: Lines added to test files divided by lines added to non-test code in recent commits.
so_what: Below 0.5 means more code shipped than test coverage — a TDD deficit. NORMS §3: failing test before logic, always.

insight.warn_msg: Test coverage lagging — new code outpacing tests.

label: file thrash
definition: Fraction of touched files that were modified in more than one commit in recent history — the rewrite/rework noise signal.
so_what: High thrash means the same files are rewritten repeatedly. This is wasted churn that NORMS §1 targets: get it right the first time.

insight.warn_msg: High file thrash — many files rewritten multiple times recently.

label: diff churn
definition: Total lines added plus deleted across recent commits — the raw diff size signal.
so_what: Large diffs are harder to review, more likely to hide bugs, and more expensive to revert. Smaller, focused changes are the NORMS §1 target.

insight.warn_msg: Large diff — consider splitting the change into focused units.

label: IJW score
definition: 0–100 composite of one-shot success rate, cache-hit, zero-bloat score, and low rework. The headline 'it just works' signal for the fleet.
so_what: The single number that proves the fleet is working correctly and efficiently. Below 60 means something systemic is wrong — the sub-metrics show where.

insight.warn_msg: IJW score low — check one-shot rate, cache-hit, and rework count.

label: one-shot %
definition: Percentage of ticket threads that closed with zero rework events — no REVISED, CHALLENGE, REJECT, or ESCALATE.
so_what: The cleanest proof that agents get it right first time. Low one-shot rate is expensive: each retry pays context re-read cost plus API cost.

insight.warn_msg: Over half of tickets needed rework — first-pass quality is low.

label: autonomy %
definition: Percentage of bus traffic that flowed agent-to-agent without a human-in-the-loop message or CONVERSE event.
so_what: High autonomy means the fleet self-coordinates. Low autonomy signals excessive human intervention or agents that can't proceed without hand-holding.

insight.warn_msg: Low autonomy — humans intervening frequently. Check for stuck agents or trust gaps.

label: $/ticket
definition: Total API cost divided by number of resolved ticket threads — the unit economics of fleet output.
so_what: Rising $/ticket is the early warning that rework, idle runs, or cold cache is eroding leverage. The trend matters more than the absolute value.

insight.warn_msg: High cost per ticket — investigate rework, cold-cache, or runaway runs.

label: open CC violations
definition: Count of functions currently exceeding the cyclomatic complexity ceiling (CC > 10), as detected by the Optimizer agent on merge.
so_what: Each violation is complexity debt. NORMS §1: optimal complexity is the bar. Open violations mean real risk of bugs hiding in hard-to-test high-CC paths.

insight.warn_msg: Open complexity violations — extract helpers to reduce CC to ≤10.

label: challenge rate
definition: Fleet-average share of ReviewVerdict messages that are CHALLENGE events — the critical review signal.
so_what: Near-zero challenge rate is a rubber-stamp smell (NORMS §3 verify duty). Sustained high rate means recurring upstream quality issues.

insight.warn_msg: Challenge rate very low — verify duty may not be active. Near-zero is the rubber-stamp smell.

label: cited accepts %
definition: Share of ACCEPT verdicts that recorded a non-empty verified[] list — proof that the reviewer reproduced the claim.
so_what: Unverified accepts (empty verified[]) are bare approvals, which PM discipline forbids. Low % means reviews are cursory, not reproductive.

insight.warn_msg: Many accepts lack evidence. Per norms: no bare approvals — empty verified[] is a defect.

label: context saved
definition: Total input tokens removed by Librarian compaction across all agents — the cumulative working-set reduction.
so_what: Every token the Librarian removes is a token not re-billed on the next turn. This directly reduces burn rate and improves cache-hit ratio.

insight.warn_msg: Librarian saving few tokens — agents may not be compacting or the daemon is idle.

label: snipped %
definition: Share of episodic context spans that were filed to the cabinet (snipped) rather than kept in the active working set.
so_what: Low snipped % means agents are carrying bloated histories. The Librarian exists to keep the working set lean — if it's not snipping, contexts bloat.

insight.warn_msg: Librarian snipping little — agents may be carrying unnecessarily large contexts.

label: context recalls
definition: Number of context recall lookups the Librarian has served — how often agents retrieve previously filed context.
so_what: Low recall count with high compaction means the Librarian is filing but nothing is being retrieved — recall pathways may be underused or broken.

insight.warn_msg: Zero recalls — filed context is not being retrieved. Check recall integration.

label: Tokens Removed
definition: Total tokens removed from context by the Librarian agent across all compaction events in this session.
so_what: More removed tokens with high precision means the Librarian is trimming efficiently — correct things removed. High removed_tokens with low precision signals over-snipping: wrong content is being cut, forcing future recalls.

label: Recalls
definition: Total number of recall events triggered during this session — each recall means a previously snipped context item was needed again.
so_what: A recall is a MISS: the Librarian removed something that was subsequently needed. High recall count means context was over-snipped — wrong things removed. Zero recalls is optimal.

label: Recalls / Compaction
definition: Average recalls per compaction event: total recalls divided by total compactions.
so_what: Normalises recall rate to compaction volume. A rising ratio means the Librarian is systematically snipping relevant content — not a one-off miss but a pattern. Near zero is healthy.

label: Precision
definition: Fraction of removed tokens that were correctly removed (not subsequently recalled): precision = 1 - (recalled_tokens / removed_tokens).
so_what: Precision is the Librarian quality score. 1.0 = perfect — nothing removed was needed again. Below 0.85 = context over-snipped: wrong things cut, forcing recalls that add latency and token cost.

label: Recalls by Role
definition: Per-agent recall counts: how many recalls each agent role triggered during this session.
so_what: Surfaces which agents are driving recalls. An agent with disproportionately high recall count indicates its working context is being over-snipped — the Librarian may be misclassifying that agent's relevant content as removable.

insight.warn_msg: One or more agent roles triggered recalls — check per-role breakdown for outliers

label: Ideal Mode
definition: Indicator of ideal Librarian operation: 1 when precision >= 0.9 and removed_tokens > 0; 0 otherwise. Re-modelled from boolean (cabinet.py:339) as count 0/1.
so_what: Ideal mode = high removed_tokens AND precision >= 0.9. Confirms the Librarian is aggressively and accurately pruning context. When 0: either pruning too conservative (low removed_tokens) or too imprecise (precision < 0.9).
